text:
**Best fit for a weekend tent-camping kit: [BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100W solar panel](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2-100w-solar-kit).** It’s a compact, modest-capacity setup: **288Wh** battery and **600W** inverter. The review says that’s enough for roughly 20 phone charges, a laptop for about 15 hours, or one night of CPAP use without humidification; in good sun, the panel can refill it in around four hours. It was listed at **$489.99** when reviewed, so check the current price and stock. ([Dealectric review and kit](https://dealectric.com/best-solar-generator-kit-for-tent-camping))

That’s a good match for phones, lights, and other small electronics—not a roomy power source for running high-draw gear all weekend. If you want substantially more battery capacity and don’t mind carrying about **24 lb**, consider the [Jackery Solar Generator 1000 v2 with 200W panel](https://www.newworldsurvival.com/reviews/solar-generator-kit.html): it has **1,070Wh** and a larger panel, but is a bigger, heavier setup. ([New World Survival review](https://www.newworldsurvival.com/reviews/solar-generator-kit.html))

judge.top_pick: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W Solar Panel Kit
